Venous return pathways (jugular veins, superior/inferior vena cava, hepatic veins): Elevated right‑atrial pressure transmits back to the jugular veins (raised JVP) and hepatic veins (congestive hepatomegaly).

snip.t: Vascular Access: Temporary non-tunnelled double-lumen central venous catheter (internal jugular vein preferred; femoral vein acceptable for emergency bed-bound patients; avoid subclavian vein to preserve future arteriovenous fistula sites).
*Answer:* The right internal jugular vein should be chosen because it provides a straight anatomical path to the right atrium and lowest complication rates.
Pressure changes in the right atrium can therefore be transmitted backwards into the jugular veins.
